title: Streaming seams must drain output and preserve execution requirements
summary: Complete subprocess output before success, propagate partial-stream failure, and carry language from selection to execution.
reusable_steps: Complete subprocess output before success, propagate partial-stream failure, and carry language from selection to execution
expected_outcome: For subprocess-backed streaming STT/TTS, child exit is not stdout EOF. Observe close, drain queued output on normal completion, and reject consumers on worker, spawn or input-source failure, including consumers waiting for their next chunk. A partial final transcript does not make a failed stream successful: propagate the failure to the batch fallback and observe early promise rejections. Pass language per transcription through normal, replay, barge-in and calibration paths; normalize it only at the worker boundary without changing process-wide environment. Verify with real subprocess fixtures, slow consumers and final-then-failure recovery tests.
